nodes.name: Turing Test (Imitation Game)
nodes.summary: Operational test of a machine's ability to exhibit intelligent behavior indistinguishable from that of a human.

nodes.name: Artificial Intelligence
nodes.summary: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems capable of performing tasks requiring human intelligence.

nodes.name: Perceptron
nodes.summary: Early artificial neuron algorithm for binary classification utilizing linear threshold units.

nodes.name: Backpropagation
nodes.summary: Algorithm for efficiently computing gradient of loss function with respect to weights in multi-layer neural networks.

nodes.name: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
nodes.summary: Feedforward neural architecture using convolution filters and spatial pooling, specialized for grid-like data such as images.

nodes.name: Deep Learning
nodes.summary: Class of machine learning algorithms that use multiple layers of representation to extract higher-level features from raw input.

nodes.name: Self-Attention Mechanism
nodes.summary: Mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence to compute a contextual representation of the sequence.

nodes.name: Transformer Architecture
nodes.summary: Sequence-to-sequence model relying entirely on self-attention without recurrence or convolutions.

nodes.name: Bidirectional Masked Language Modeling
nodes.summary: Pre-training objective conditioning on both left and right context across all transformer layers simultaneously.

nodes.name: Autoregressive Large Language Models
nodes.summary: Decoder-only generative transformer models scaled to billions of parameters demonstrating emergent in-context few-shot capabilities.

edges.description: Perceptron developed as foundational algorithmic attempt toward realizing the artificial intelligence agenda.

The representational limitations of single-layer perceptrons, demonstrated by Minsky and Papert, directly influenced the development of multi-layer learning algorithms, leading to the popularization of backpropagation by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams.
Convolutional neural networks (such as LeNet) use backpropagation and gradient-based learning to train shared spatial convolution kernels directly from input pixels.
GPU-accelerated deep convolutional network (AlexNet) victory at ImageNet 2012 ignited modern deep learning renaissance.
Transformer architecture was introduced by replacing recurrent computation entirely with multi-head self-attention.
Bidirectional language models such as BERT extend the Transformer encoder architecture with masked language pre-training to learn context from both left and right directions simultaneously.
Autoregressive large language models (such as GPT-3) use the causal decoder variant of the Transformer architecture, scaled to massive parameter and token counts.
